page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processors running at 3.525 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is sized at 512.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. A key architectural characteristic of this server type is its 16,047 GB of directly attached local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate high multi-threaded compute capability and robust I/O throughput. The instance recorded top-tier throughput in PassMark memory testing (3105.5), alongside strong multi-core processing scores in stress-ng (86390.68) and PassMark CPU evaluations (63250.48). Database operations scored strongly under PassMark testing at 26,338.98, reinforced by Redis SET transaction rates reaching 63.44 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 299.52 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded execution, static web serving, and uncached large-block memory read/write bandwidth performed within median baseline ranges.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the substantial consolidation of 16 TB of local NVMe storage with 512 GB of system memory reduces total platform footprint by eliminating the overhead of auxiliary external block storage volumes for throughput-intensive setups. The architecture trades off high single-core peak clocks and specialized vector extensions like AVX-512 in exchange for extensive high-bandwidth storage capacity and distributed core density. Microsoft Azure L64as_v3 is suited for large-scale relational databases, NoSQL data stores, distributed caching layers, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput transactional systems.
description: Microsoft Azure L64as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor at 3.525 GHz and 512.0 GB of system memory. Designed for I/O-intensive workloads, it bundles 16,047 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show upper-quartile multi-core processing capacity, top-decile memory performance, and strong key-value database throughput reaching 63.44 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded speed and uncached large-block bandwidth operate at median levels, the high density of direct NVMe capacity delivers efficient local storage consolidation. This instance configuration is suitable for large operational databases, transactional systems, distributed caching, and big data data stores.
